the_refusals_in_order.fix: the operator role is set explicitly to the read-only 'gateway status' role, which the product's ordinary gateway contract admits

the_blocking_mechanism.the_rule: plugins/friday_rework/onboarding.py _admitted_worker_home() (line 795) requires the profile's own settings to have runtime == {'enabled': False} and NO worker_requirements; otherwise it raises ordinary_worker_free_home_required
the_blocking_mechanism.who_calls_it: Onboarding.qualify_workers() calls _worker_attachment() (line 1086) for a bound principal, and _worker_attachment() calls _admitted_worker_home() first
the_blocking_mechanism.how_the_profile_got_that_way: Onboarding.prepare() writes worker_requirements = ['dsh','a0'] into the profile
whenever the template carries worker_inputs (line 516), and Onboarding.qualify_workers() writes it again for a
bound principal (line 1135) together with runtime = {'enabled': True, ...} (line 1134).
Both user areas are in that state now: telegram-bot-8812646969 and dest_telegram both have runtime.enabled = true
the_blocking_mechanism.the_consequence: a profile that already carries its workers can no longer be qualified, archived or reconciled
through the product: archive_workers() calls the same _admitted_worker_home() (line 991) and is refused the same
way. The product's own state read confirms it: worker_execution =
dsh and a0 are RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED / qualified = false.
the_blocking_mechanism.the_way_out_that_the_product_offers: a fresh area prepared with the ordinary template and then prepared and
qualified in that order. That means a NEW user area, which is a re-preparation of a user and is explicitly out
of scope for the current work: the working profiles are kept and the access row, the binding and the access
history are never deleted to get past the refusal.

a0_qualification.what_is_not_claimed: no A0 qualification result, no stop and no retirement are claimed; the 13 historical INITIAL_PROBE_RETIRED receipts and the empty container table remain what they were
